title: Kernel hotspot annotator with phase-aware session splitter and weighted-sample pruning
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We need more structured, phase-aware profiling outputs to detect regressions that only manifest in specific sequence phases (prompting, KV warmup, decoding, postprocess). Existing baseline exporters aggregate across entire sessions which dilutes kernel-level hotpaths that occur briefly but drive tail latency. This PR introduces a lightweight, offline-only 'kernel hotspot annotator' plus a phase-aware session splitter and an optional weighted-sample pruning stage so downstream reporters see clearer signals without increasing runtime overhead.

What this change does: Adds three cooperating components: (1) phase-aware session splitter: annotates raw traces with sequence-phase boundaries (heuristics based on token-type markers and timing gaps) and emits per-phase sub-sessions; (2) kernel hotspot annotator: processes per-phase traces to attribute time spent to kernel groups (matmul, attention-kv, softmax, memory-copy) and annotates frames with kernel tags suitable for flamegraph and histogram exporters; (3) weighted-sample pruning: an adaptive sampling pass that downweights noisy samples (short cold-start traces) while preserving rare high-cost tails by boosting their sample weight. Outputs are JSONL records and a compact CSV summary designed to feed the regression-detector pipeline.

Compatibility and scope: All changes are offline-only and additive. No serving runtime or hot paths are changed. The new annotator can be toggled via the bench config (bench_config.phase_annotation = true) and a feature flag for canary jobs. Default is off for general runs; enabled by default in the new 'phase-hotspot' benchmark profile.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for phase boundary detection and kernel attribution were added. End-to-end validation was run against the 'seqmix-2024q4' baseline corpus (10k sessions). We compared metric stability (p50/p95/p99) with and without pruning; pruning reduced noise in p99 variance while preserving mean estimates. CI includes a smoke run of the new profile that produces a sample flamegraph artifact.

Release notes: Adds a new offline annotator and a benchmark profile 'phase-hotspot' for kernel-level regression detection. No breaking changes.

Checklist:
- [x] Phase splitter implementation and tests
- [x] Kernel annotator and unit tests
- [x] Weighted-sample pruning algorithm and integration
- [x] Reporting pipeline adapter (CSV + JSONL)
- [x] Bench profile + CI smoke job

How to use: Enable bench_config.phase_annotation = true in bench config or run the included shim benchctl run --profile phase-hotspot --output ./out to produce annotated traces + CSV summary. Follow the README additions for interpreting annotated fields and mapping kernel tags to flamegraph rows.

Related work: complements ENG-1049 (kv-cache-trace-normalizer) and ENG-1187 (regression-detector improvements).

feat: kernel hotspot annotator; kernel group attribution and flamegraph tagging
chore: weighted-sample pruning algorithm and deterministic seed for reproducible runs
ci: add smoke job and artifact upload for phase-hotspot profile
docs: update benchmark-lab README with new profile and usage examples
review_thread: Ravi Patel: Nice approach; can you clarify how phases are detected when token markers are absent?
Maya Chen: We fall back to a timing-gap heuristic (threshold configurable) and prefer conservative splits to avoid over-segmentation.
Clara Nuñez: Sampling looks good but could bias rare regressions if weights are not clipped — please add upper bound.
Maya Chen: Added a clip parameter (max_sample_weight) and altered tests to cover it.
Jules Park: CI artifact upload failed on first run (timeout). Re-ran and everything passed. Approved.
Ravi Patel: Approved after the pruning clip was added; please add a short blurb to the benchmark-lab README about interpreting weighted counts.
ci_flaky_notes: integration-smoke initially timed out on artifact upload; retry succeeded. no code changes between runs.
release_notes: Added a phase-aware offline annotator and a new 'phase-hotspot' benchmark profile that emits kernel-level flamegraph tags and CSV summaries for regression detection. No runtime changes; opt-in via bench config.
notes: This PR seeds the regression-detector with higher-fidelity signals for kernel-level regressions. Recommend scheduling nightly phase-hotspot runs for 2 weeks to establish stable baselines before enabling alerts.
